summary: Utah mother of six and YouTube parenting influencer Ruby Franke pleaded guilty to child abuse charges for torturing her two youngest children while trying to convince them they were evil and possessed. The plea agreement details the abuse of her 12-year-old son and 9-year-old daughter, carried out with co-defendant Jodi Hildebrandt. Sentencing is set for Feb. 20, and her attorneys blame Hildebrandt's influence.
one_line: YouTube parenting influencer Ruby Franke pleaded guilty to aggravated child abuse of her two youngest children, with sentencing set for Feb. 20.
key_facts: Ruby Franke, a Utah mother of six who gave parenting advice on YouTube, pleaded guilty Monday to child abuse charges.
Judge John J. Walton scheduled sentencing for Feb. 20 after accepting the plea agreement; sentences will run consecutively and sentencing is up to the judge.
Franke pleaded guilty to four counts and not guilty to two other counts, and was returned to custody.
Under Utah law, each charge of second-degree aggravated child abuse carries a sentence of one to 15 years in prison.
Franke admitted torturing her son from May 22 through Aug. 30 with forced physical tasks, outdoor work without adequate water, blistering sunburns, food denial and isolation.
After her son tried to run away in July, his hands and feet were regularly bound, sometimes with handcuffs and ropes.
Franke also admitted kicking her son while wearing boots, holding his head under water and smothering his mouth and nose.
Franke admitted similarly abusing her 9-year-old daughter, who was told she was evil and possessed and was forced to run barefoot on dirt roads and go without food and water.
Franke and Jodi Hildebrandt were arrested on Aug. 30 after Franke's 12-year-old son escaped from Hildebrandt's house in Ivins, Utah, and asked a neighbor to call police.
The boy was emaciated with duct tape around his ankles and wrists; Franke's four youngest children were taken into state custody.
Franke and Hildebrandt were each charged with six felony counts of aggravated child abuse and have remained jailed since their arrests.
Winward Law said Franke was influenced by Hildebrandt, a relationship counselor, who gave her 'a distorted sense of morality'.
Hildebrandt agreed not to see patients until state licensing officials address the allegations; her next hearing is Dec. 27.
The '8 Passengers' YouTube channel started in 2015 and ended after seven years; Franke's husband, Kevin Franke, has filed for divorce.
